record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: For a general polygon P, find nontrivial upper and lower bounds for billiard complexity, such as the growth of the number of admissible coding words of length at most n for billiard orbits in P.

evidence.quote: Задача 14. Найти нетривиальные верхнюю и нижнюю оценки сложности биллиардов для общих многоугольников.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygon (not necessarily rational), and consider the billiard flow inside $P$: a point particle moves along straight lines inside $P$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) off the sides, with trajectories that hit a vertex declared undefined. Label the sides of $P$ by symbols from a finite alphabet $\mathcal{A}$ whose letters correspond to the sides of $P$. To each (one-sided) billiard trajectory associate the infinite word over $\mathcal{A}$ recording the sequence of sides hit by successive reflections. The billiard complexity function $p_P(n)$ is defined as the number of distinct admissible words of length $n$ that occur as factors of the codings of billiard orbits in $P$.

Problem. For a general polygon $P$, establish nontrivial upper and lower bounds on $p_P(n)$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, determine explicit functions $f(n)$ and $g(n)$ (going beyond the trivial subexponential bound and beyond bounds known only for special classes such as rational polygons) such that
$$ f(n) \;\le\; p_P(n) \;\le\; g(n) $$
for all sufficiently large $n$, valid for an arbitrary polygon $P$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known. Cassaigne–Hubert–Troubetzkoy (2002) related word complexity to the count of generalized diagonals and obtained cubic upper and lower bounds in the rational case (with cubic asymptotic in the tiling case). Recent work (2023–2025, e.g., "On the complexity of polygonal billiards") shows that for a typical polygon the complexity grows cubically and obtains polynomial bounds on slow entropy. However, sharp nontrivial upper and lower bounds for fully general (in particular, irrational) polygons remain not completely established, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Complexity and growth for polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Cubic upper and lower bounds for complexity in the rational case; cubic asymptotic growth in the tiling case.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial (cubic) bounds for billiard complexity are known in the rational/tiling case.

status_evidence.title: On the complexity of polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: For a typical polygon, the complexity grows cubically and the number of saddle connections grows quadratically along subsequences.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results give cubic complexity growth for typical polygons.

status_evidence.title: Complexity lower bounds for polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes polynomial lower bounds for complexity of polygonal billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds on billiard complexity have been obtained.
